writeup: TIC 272854495 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 1.7151 days. Observations from TESS photometry show a primary eclipse causing a 5.03 percent dimming of the star's light, detected with a signal-to-noise ratio of 621.8 using the Box Least Squares algorithm. Pixel-level image analysis confirms the signal originates from the target location, with a peak signal-to-noise of 20.2, though the centroid offset of 2.7 arcseconds warrants attention in any future observations. No secondary eclipse was detected in the available data. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, suggesting it may not have been previously cataloged. The automated pipeline assigned this target a machine-learning screening score of 0.66, indicating moderate confidence that this represents a genuine eclipsing binary system rather than a false positive.
